newsitem.title: MOROCCO: More than 13 million voters to vote in June.
newsitem.headline: More than 13 million voters to vote in June.

text.p: More than 13 million voters or nearly half Morocco's population will be called on June 13 to elect members of 1,600 communal and municipal councils, the interior ministry said on Wednesday.
Interior Minister Driss Basri announced earlier that Morocco, will hold local council elections on June 13 and campaigning would start on May 29 and close on June 12.
"According to the latest official figures more than 13 million voters will participate in the communal and municipal elections of June 13, 1997," an interior ministry official told Reuters.
An estimated 24,000 councillors will be elected, the official said but gave no other details.
In principle, the councils will later elect representatives to about 80 percent of seats in a new Upper House of parliament being set up under constitutional reforms approved last September.

Details on the exact number of councillors and configuration of the new parliament are expected to be announced soon after the appointment by King Hassan of an independent multi-party body to supervise the elections, a Moroccan political analyst said.
Voting will be held throughout the country, including the disputed Western Sahara territory, the analyst said.

The local elections are the first of a series which will culminate in parliamentary elections in September, with a new bicameral parliament being inaugurated by King Hassan on the second Friday of October.
Under the new constitution, the lower house of parliament will be directly elected by universal suffrage, with the upper house being mainly elected indirectly.
The upper house will have power to vote a no-confidence motion in the government and legally overthrow it.
The present 333-seat parliament is composed of a majority centre-right parties, while opposition led by the old-guard Istiqlal party hold 125 seats only.
